claims.text: As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness and strength.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi is a fully disordered, single-phase solid solution with minimal nanoscale obstacles to dislocation motion.
The absence of SRO regions or coherent nanoscale precipitates governs the alloy's low hardness and strength by allowing easier dislocation motion.
Aging at approximately 600 °C for 10 hours will induce SRO regions or coherent nanoprecipitates in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Control of the aging ramp and cooling rate can produce fine, uniform ordering or nanoprecipitates while avoiding coarse or heterogeneous precipitation.
SRO creates resistance to slip and increases dislocation-glide resistance.
Fine coherent precipitates can strengthen an alloy by acting as obstacles to dislocation motion.
The as-cast CoCrFeNiTi solid solution has relatively high stacking-fault energy.
Relatively high stacking-fault energy in the starting alloy facilitates unobstructed dislocation glide.
Unobstructed dislocation glide causes low work hardening and minimal strengthening in the as-cast alloy.
Aging-induced localized ordering will pin dislocations.
The induced nanoscale obstacles will increase dislocation pile-up.
The induced nanoscale obstacles will produce a higher strain-hardening rate.
The aged alloy will have higher yield strength than the as-cast alloy.
The aged alloy will have higher hardness than the as-cast alloy.
TEM and diffraction will reveal fine, uniformly distributed SRO regions or coherent precipitates after aging.
The proposed comparison keeps the equimolar CoCrFeNiTi composition unchanged and applies identical room-temperature tensile and compression tests at a fixed moderate strain rate.
The hypothesis is limited to equimolar or near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi and to aging conditions that avoid coarse precipitation.

contradictions.description: The mediator permits formation of coherent nanoprecipitates, which ordinarily implies a distinct precipitate phase, while the boundary says the alloy must remain single-phase. The SRO alternative is compatible with that boundary, but the coherent-precipitate alternative is not clearly compatible.
